A write-ahead log is a file that contains a record of all changes made to the database. When a change is made to the database, the change is first written to the log, and then the change is written to the database itself. This ensures that the log always contains a complete and accurate record of all changes made to the database, even if the database itself is corrupted or lost.
When a database crashes, the write-ahead log can be used to recover the database to a consistent state. The log is scanned to determine the last consistent point in the database, and all changes made after that point are discarded. The database is then rebuilt from the log, using the changes recorded in the log to update the database to the last consistent point. This ensures that the database is recovered to a consistent state, even if the database itself is corrupted or lost.
The write-ahead log also provides a way to recover from partial failures, such as a power outage that causes the database to shut down unexpectedly. In this case, the log can be used to determine the last consistent point in the database, and the database can be recovered to that point. This ensures that the database is recovered to a consistent state, even if the database itself is partially corrupted or lost.
